Non-zero application code. Which code is possible depends on the HTTP
status — the error table in the introduction is the complete mapping.

Optional, and used by **one** failure only: a scope denial (`403` with code
`12015`) carries `required_scope` here, naming the scope the key lacks.

The fetch service's explanation, present only for the codes marked in the

info.description:
One API key for the four retrieval capabilities (extract, template, search, map)
plus change monitoring (watch), all running on flowda's fetch network.

* **Base URL** — the host this documentation is served from
  (production: `https://openapi.flowda.ai`).
* **Response body** — every capability endpoint returns the fetch platform's own
  response body, projected verbatim into `data`. Field names and semantics therefore
  match the platform contract; the only exception is that internal fields
  (for example `meta.snapshot_id`, the platform's snapshot storage path) are **removed**.

## Credentials

Three credential forms are accepted, all of them scoped to your account:

| How | Header | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `Authorization: Bearer flw_<env>_<key_id>_<secret>` | Created in the console. Per-endpoint `scope` is enforced. |
| API key | `X-API-Key: <key>` | Equivalent form; `Authorization` wins when both are present. |
| Session | `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` or the `flowda_token` cookie | Obtained by signing in to the console. A session is the account owner, so **scopes are not enforced**. |

Scopes: `extract` (extract, template, templates), `search`, `map`, `watch`.
A key that lacks a scope gets **403 with code 12015** (not 401) — the credential is
valid, the grant is not; `data.required_scope` names the scope you need.
`GET /v1/account` tells you which scopes your key carries.

## Response envelope

Success — HTTP 200, `code` is `0`:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "success",
  "request_id": "req_6a99053110d62d17",
  "data": {
    "success": true,
    "request_id": "req_01K7XT3B6C9D4M2Q",
    "credits_used": 1,
    "outputs": { "markdown": "# Example" },
    "meta": { "strategy_used": "X1", "cache_hit": true }
  }
}
```

Failure — the HTTP status is the one in the table below and `code` is a non-zero
application code. Every failure body has `code`, `message` and `request_id`; the
only optional members are `details` and, for a single code, `data`:

```json
{
  "code": 16002,
  "message": "the request was rejected, see details",
  "request_id": "req_6a99053110d62d17",
  "details": ["The request body is invalid(url)."]
}
```

`details` is present only for the codes marked *yes* in the error table: it carries
the reason the request failed — for 16xxx codes that is the fetch service's own
explanation (usually naming the exact field), for the rest it is ours — and it is
the fastest way to fix a rejected call.

`data` is present on **exactly one** failure: a scope denial (`403` with code
`12015`) puts the missing scope in `data.required_scope`, because that is the one
field the caller needs in order to fix the key:

```json
{
  "code": 12015,
  "message": "api key scope denied",
  "request_id": "req_6a99053110d62d17",
  "data": { "required_scope": "map" }
}
```

Every other failure omits `data`, so a failure handler must treat it as optional
rather than required or forbidden.

## ⚠️ Check `data.success`, not just the status code

The fetch platform reports "the target could not be retrieved" **inside a 200
response**: HTTP 200, outer `code: 0`, but `data.success: false` with a platform
code and message:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "success",
  "request_id": "req_a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
  "data": {
    "success": false,
    "code": "TARGET_DNS_ERROR",
    "message": "The target host could not be resolved.",
    "request_id": "core-req-9f2c1b"
  }
}
```

So a client must treat `data.success === false` as a failed call even though the
status is 200. (The same rule is applied to your call log: such a call is recorded
as **failed**, with the platform code and reason attached.)
`data.success` is always present for capability calls.

### What `data.code` can contain

`data.code` is an uppercase string owned by the fetch service. The lists below are
the codes that endpoint can currently produce; anything else should be handled like
`UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

**extract** — `TARGET_TIMEOUT`, `TARGET_DNS_ERROR` (the host, or a redirect target,
could not be resolved), `TARGET_SSL_ERROR`, `TARGET_SITE_ERROR` (unreachable,
redirect loop, invalid redirect, non-routable address), `TARGET_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED`
(every retrieval engine failed, or the page has no readable content — a
JavaScript-only page also lands here: retry with `advanced_mode`),
`TARGET_UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE` (the target is a file type we do not deliver),
`UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

**template** — `TARGET_SITE_ERROR`, `TARGET_DNS_ERROR`, `TARGET_TIMEOUT`,
`TARGET_SSL_ERROR`, `TARGET_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED`, `TEMPLATE_MISMATCH` (the page no
longer matches the template contract), `UNKNOWN_ERROR`. A missing product or an
empty listing is *not* one of these: it comes back as a success with
`outputs: null` and is still billed.

**map** — `INVALID_REQUEST`, `INVALID_API_KEY`, `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS`,
`RATE_LIMITED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `TARGET_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED`, `TARGET_TIMEOUT`,
`UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

**search** — a per-result extraction failure is reported inside
`data.outputs[].extract` (`success: false` on that result) and does not fail the call;
a platform-level failure uses this shape like every other capability endpoint.

Two extract rejections use the HTTP status line instead of `data.success`, and arrive
with `16002`: `EXTRACTION_SELECTION_EMPTY` (your `exclude_tags` removed all body text)
and `EXTRACTION_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE` (the parser output exceeded the resource budget —
reduce `formats`).

## Two request identifiers — quote both in a support request

| Value | Who generated it | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request_id` (envelope) | flowda | Envelope of every response, success or failure |
| `request_id` inside `data` | the fetch platform | Platform response body; identical to the `X-Upstream-Request-Id` response header |

For `POST /v1/map` the value inside `data` may be the fetch network's own identifier
instead of the platform's; the `X-Upstream-Request-Id` header is the authoritative
one when you need to trace a single call.

## Error codes

| code | HTTP | Meaning | What to do | `details` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10000 | 500 | Internal error | Retry later; contact us if it persists | no |
| 11000 | 400 | Invalid request | Fix the request as described in `details` | yes |
| 11004 | 404 | Not found | Check the path; jobs and checks must belong to your account | no |
| 11005 | 405 | Method not allowed | Use the documented method | no |
| 12001 | 401 | Authentication required | Send an API key or a session token | no |
| 12002 | 401 | Invalid or expired session token | Sign in again | no |
| 12003 | 403 | Forbidden | Account disabled, or the write request failed its origin check | no |
| 12014 | 401 | API key invalid, revoked or expired | Check the key in the console | no |
| 12015 | 403 | API key lacks this endpoint's scope | Add the scope named in `data.required_scope` | no |
| 13000 | 429 | Rate limit exceeded | Back off using `Retry-After` | no |
| 13002 | 402 | Daily quota exhausted | Wait for the next UTC day, or ask us for a higher quota | yes |
| 14000 | 500 | Storage unavailable | Retry later; contact us if it persists | no |
| 16000 | 502 | The fetch service failed | Retry later | no |
| 16001 | 504 | The fetch service did not answer in time | Retry later | no |
| 16002 | 400 | The fetch service rejected the request | Fix the request as described in `details` | yes |
| 16003 | 429 | The fetch service is rate limiting | Reduce concurrency and retry | no |
| 16004 | 402 | The fetch service has no credits left | Contact us to top up | yes |
| 16005 | 503 | The fetch service is unreachable | Retry later | no |
| 16006 | 400 | `webhook_url` rejected | Fix the URL as described in `details` | yes |
| 16007 | 401 | Webhook signature invalid | Only returned on the platform callback endpoint | no |
| 16008 | 409 | Conflicts with the job's current state | Adjust the state; `details` says which conflict | yes |
| 16009 | 500 | Configuration problem on our side | **Contact us — retrying will not help** | no |

Codes in the 16xxx range describe the fetch service. `16009` means *our* platform
credential is broken (a flowda-side configuration fault), never your API key:
it is deliberately not a 401 so that you do not go looking for a problem in your
own credentials.

## Form-encoded request bodies

Endpoints that accept both `application/json` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
use the same field names for both media types. Form-encoded bodies are converted to
JSON before processing, so all validation and field rules apply identically.

### Encoding rules

- **Strings**: send as a single value. Repeating the same field name for scalar fields
  returns `400` with code `11000`.
- **Booleans**: only `true` and `false` are accepted (as literal strings, unquoted).
- **Integers**: decimal notation only; no leading zeros or decimal points (`01`, `1.0` rejected).
- **Arrays**: repeat the field name (`formats=markdown&formats=links`), or send a JSON
  array as a single string value (`formats=["markdown","links"]`). If the value starts
  with `[` but is not valid JSON (for example, the CSS selector `[data-kind]`), it is
  treated as a regular string element in a single-item array.
- **Objects** (`headers`, `extract_options`, `params`): send as a JSON object string
  (`headers={"Accept-Language":"en-US"}`).
- **Empty values**: a field sent with an empty value (`include_tags=`) means "not
  provided" — it is dropped before the request is forwarded, exactly as if you had
  left the field out. Send `include_tags=[]` if you really need an empty array.
- **Character encoding**: UTF-8 only. A `charset` parameter other than `utf-8` or a
  body that is not valid UTF-8 after percent-decoding returns `400` with code `11000`.

Unknown fields are accepted and forwarded — the fetch service will reject them with a
specific field message if they are not recognized. This matches the JSON behavior.

**Example**:

```
POST /v1/extract HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com&formats=markdown&formats=links&only_main_content=false&max_age_ms=0&headers=%7B%22Accept-Language%22%3A%22en-US%22%7D
```

is equivalent to:

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com",
  "formats": ["markdown", "links"],
  "only_main_content": false,
  "max_age_ms": 0,
  "headers": {"Accept-Language": "en-US"}
}
```

## Billing

* Every call to a capability endpoint is billed once it reaches the fetch service.
  **There is no idempotency key**, so a retry after a timeout can be billed twice —
  confirm the outcome in your call log before retrying.
* `credits_used` in the response reports what this call cost:
  extract costs 1 credit on a cache hit and 1 / 3 / 5 by the strategy used on a miss;
  template execution costs a flat 5 credits (a successful but empty result still
  costs 5, a failed execution costs 0); search is billed per result.
* `GET /v1/templates` and `GET /v1/templates/{template_id}` are metadata calls:
  they cost 0 credits but still appear in your call log.
* `render_js` is an internal troubleshooting switch of the fetch service and is
  **not exposed** — use `advanced_mode` when a page needs rendering.
* A request that carries your own `headers` never reads the platform's snapshot
  cache, and the target URL stays marked for 48 hours. Do not send `headers` for
  private pages you do not want to be re-fetched.

## Availability

The whole `/v1/**` surface (capabilities, `GET /v1/account`, this documentation and
everything under `/v1/watch`) shares a single server-side switch. When the operator
has it off, **every** `/v1` route answers `404` with code `11004` — that is a
deliberate, uniform state, not a routing mistake. `GET /api/v1/healthz` and
`GET /api/v1/readyz` stay available either way.
info.title: flowda Developer API

get.description:
Answers "who am I, what may I call, how much is left" from the already-resolved
credential — it never queries the database, so it keeps working while you
diagnose a 403.

Rules worth knowing:

* `key_id` is empty for session calls.
* `scopes` is an empty array for session calls: a session is the account owner
  and is not restricted by scopes.
* `scope_enforced` is `true` only for API key calls.

post.description:
Fetches one URL and returns the representations you ask for. Accepts JSON or
form-encoded bodies (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`); the same field names
apply to both.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | **yes** | — | absolute `http`/`https` URL | The page to fetch. The host, every redirect hop and every resolved address must be public — loopback, private, link-local and reserved ranges are rejected. |
| `formats` | string[] | no | `["markdown"]` | `markdown`, `raw_html`, `clean_html`, `links` (no duplicates) | Which representations to produce. Only the keys you ask for are returned. |
| `only_main_content` | boolean | no | `true` | — | Keep the article body only, dropping navigation, footers and sidebars. |
| `include_tags` | string[] | no | — | CSS selectors | Keep only nodes matching these selectors. |
| `exclude_tags` | string[] | no | — | CSS selectors | Remove matching nodes. If this removes all body text the call returns `400 EXTRACTION_SELECTION_EMPTY` — adjust the selectors and retry. |
| `max_age_ms` | integer | no | `172800000` (2 days) | `0 … 172800000` | How old a cached snapshot may be. `0` forces a fresh fetch. |
| `headers` | object<string,string> | no | — | e.g. `{"Accept-Language":"en-US"}` | Headers forwarded to the target site. `Host` and hop-by-hop headers are rejected. See the cache-isolation side effect in the introduction. |
| `wait_for_ms` | integer | no | `0` | `0 … 30000`, and at most half of `timeout_ms` | Extra wait after the page has loaded. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | no | `60000` | `1000 … 120000` | Budget for the whole call: validation, fetch, rendering and extraction. |
| `country` | string | no | `US` | two letters from the supported egress regions | Access region. A well-formed code outside the list is rejected. |
| `advanced_mode` | boolean | no | `true` | — | `true` lets the fetch service escalate based on page signals; `false` keeps it on the direct engine. This is the supported way to ask for rendering. |

`render_js` is deliberately **not** accepted: it is the platform's paid browser
troubleshooting switch. Sending it returns `400` with code `11000`.

### Reading the result

* `data.success` is the call's real outcome (see the introduction).
* `data.outputs` contains exactly the formats you requested; a requested-but-empty
  `markdown` is `""`, an unproducible one is `null`.
* `data.meta.strategy_used` is `X1` / `X2` / `X3` and drives the price;
  `data.meta.cache_hit` tells you whether a snapshot was reused.
* `data.meta.result.status_code` is the **target site's** status and may be `null`
  when the fetch service could not observe one — it is not this API's status code.

data.message: The target host could not be resolved.

200.description:
Either a retrieved page or a platform-level failure inside `data`
(`data.success: false`).

post.description:
Discovers the reachable URLs of a site. Accepts JSON or form-encoded bodies.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | **yes** | — | absolute `http`/`https` URL | The site to enumerate. The host must be publicly resolvable. |
| `country` | string | no | `US` | uppercase two-letter code | Access region. |
| `domain_filter` | string | no | `all` | `domain` (same host only), `all` (include external links) | Whether off-site links are returned. |
| `limit` | integer | no | `5000` | `1 … 100000` | Upper bound on returned URLs. |
| `sitemap` | string | no | `include` | `skip`, `include`, `only` | How sitemaps are used: ignored, merged, or the only source. |

### Reading the result

* `data.outputs` is an array of `{url, title?, description?}`; it is `null` when
  nothing was discovered.
* `data.meta.result` describes the entry page: `status_code` may be `null` when
  the entry HTML was never fetched, and `url` echoes the URL you sent.
* Like the other capabilities, a failure may arrive as `data.success: false`
  inside a 200 response.

200.description: Discovered URLs, possibly a platform-level failure in `data`

get.description:
The regions you may pass as `country` to `POST /v1/extract`, `POST /v1/search`,
`POST /v1/map` and `POST /v1/watch/jobs`, with the name to show for each one.

* Only **enabled** regions are returned; a region that was taken out of service
  disappears from this list and is rejected as a `country` value.
* Every entry carries two fields: `code` (two uppercase letters, the value you
  send) and `name_en` (the English name to display).
* No pagination and no filters — the whole list is small and is meant to be cached
  by your own process if you need to, not fetched per request by the browser.
* The list is served by flowda itself, not proxied to the fetch platform.
* **No key is required**: the list carries no account information, and the
  people who need it most are the ones still setting up a credential.

200.description: All enabled regions, ordered by code

post.description:
Searches the web and optionally extracts the full content of every result in the
same call. Accepts JSON or form-encoded bodies.

Every call is written to your usage records — **including the `query` itself** — so a
failed search can be traced back to what you searched for. Retention follows your
usage-record retention (12 months by default).

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | **yes** | — | 1–256 characters | The query. |
| `max_results` | integer | no | `10` | `1 … 100` | **Upper bound, not an exact count** — fewer results are still a success. |
| `source` | string | no | `web` | `web`, `news`, `shopping`, `scholar` | Which corpus to search. `time_range` is rejected together with `shopping`/`scholar`; `country` is rejected with `scholar`. |
| `country` | string | no | — | uppercase two-letter ISO code from the supported list | Restricts results to a country. Lowercase is rejected. |
| `language` | string | no | — | lower-case language code, e.g. `en`, `zh-cn`, `pt-br` | Preferred result language. |
| `time_range` | string | no | — | `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year` | Recency filter. |
| `extract_content` | boolean | no | `false` | — | Also extract the full content of each result. |
| `extract_options` | object | no | — | only allowed when `extract_content: true` | Options for the inline extraction (see below). |

`extract_options` accepts `formats` (`markdown`, `raw_html`, `clean_html`, `links`;
no duplicates), `only_main_content`, `include_tags`, `exclude_tags`,
`advanced_mode`, `max_age_ms` (`0 … 172800000`), `timeout_ms`
(`1000 … 120000`) and `wait_for_ms` (`0 … 30000`, at most half of `timeout_ms`).
`headers`, `url` and `country` are not accepted inside `extract_options`.

It only takes effect with `extract_content: true`. When extraction is off (or the
flag is omitted) the field is dropped before the request reaches the fetch service,
so a stale, default-filled object cannot fail the call.

### Reading the result

* `data.outputs` is an array of results, each with `position`, `title`, `url`,
  `snippet` and — for `news` — a human-readable `date`.
* With `extract_content: true` every result also carries `extract`; when that
  single extraction fails it is reported per result
  (`extract.success: false` with `extract.code` / `extract.message`) while the
  search itself still succeeds.
* Zero results is a **success**: `data.outputs` is `null` and
  `data.meta.count` is `0`.

post.description:
Runs one of the published templates against a supported site and returns records
shaped by that template's output schema. Costs a flat 5 credits per execution.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | string | **yes** | — | `amazon_product`, `amazon_search`, `amazon_bestsellers`, `walmart_product`, `walmart_search`, `walmart_category` | Which template to run. The catalogue with the current set is `GET /v1/templates`. |
| `params` | object | **yes** | — | depends on the template | Template input. The exact schema — including which key identifies the item — is `data.data.params_schema` from `GET /v1/templates/{template_id}`; it describes the **whole** request body (`template` plus `params`), and unknown keys are rejected. |

Identifier key per template:

| Template | Key | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amazon_product` | `asin` | 10 uppercase letters/digits |
| `amazon_search` | `query` | 1–256 characters |
| `amazon_bestsellers` | `url` | `https://www.amazon.com/...` best-sellers ranking page |
| `walmart_product` | `item_id` | 5–15 digits |
| `walmart_search` | `query` | 1–256 characters |
| `walmart_category` | `url` | Walmart category page |

Common optional `params` keys:

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zipcode` | string | none | US 5-digit ZIP code used for pricing and availability. When omitted the target site decides the delivery location — flowda deliberately does not inject a default. |
| `pages` | integer | `1` | Which results page to collect. List templates only; sending it to a detail template is rejected. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | `60000` | Execution budget, `1000 … 120000`. |

### Reading the result

* `data.outputs` is an array of records (or `null` when there was no content);
  detail templates return one record.
* `data.meta.fields` explains the record fields **that apply to this template**,
  keyed by field path (for example `variants[].price`) — use it to render labels
  in your own UI. Descriptions are provided by the template's published schema.
* A successful but empty result is not a failure: `data.success` is `true`,
  `data.outputs` is `null`, and the 5 credits are still charged.
* A failed execution reports `data.success: false` with a platform `code`
  (for example `TEMPLATE_MISMATCH` or `TARGET_SITE_ERROR`) and is not charged.

events are sent: a check that finds no change delivers nothing, and a job
without `webhook_url` sends nothing.

Every request is signed with that job's `webhook_secret`; the Webhooks guide
lists the headers, the string that is signed and the retry rules. Read the
change itself from `data.diff`, or just its one-line summary from
`data.check.diff_summary`.

post.description:
Registers a page with a schedule and returns the job. The job is created on the
fetch platform under flowda's credential; ownership stays with your account here.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | **yes** | — | absolute `http`/`https` URL, publicly resolvable | The page to monitor. Immutable afterwards. |
| `schedule` | object | **yes** | — | `{interval_seconds}` **or** `{cron}` — exactly one | When to check. `interval_seconds` is `60 … 2592000` and runs on the UTC timeline (the timezone does not shift it); `cron` is a standard five-field expression interpreted in `timezone` (weekends included). |
| `timezone` | string | no | `UTC` | IANA timezone name | Affects `cron` schedules only. |
| `country` | string | no | `US` | two letters | Access region for the checks. |
| `selector` | string | no | — | CSS or XPath, per `selector_type` | Monitor only part of the page. |
| `selector_type` | string | no | `css` | `css`, `xpath` | How `selector` is interpreted. |
| `diff_modes` | string[] | no | `["auto"]` | `auto`, `text`, `json` (no duplicates; `auto` cannot be combined) | How differences are computed. |
| `retention_days` | integer | no | `30` | `0 … 365` | How long check history is kept; `0` means keep it indefinitely. |
| `webhook_url` | string | no | no notifications | absolute `http`/`https` URL on a public host, port 80 or 443 | Where change events are delivered. flowda rewrites it to its own relay before handing the job to the platform, and swaps your address back in the responses. |
| `headers` | object<string,string> | no | `{}` | `Host` and hop-by-hop headers are rejected | Extra headers for the checks. |
| `mask` | object | no | `{enabled: false, exclude: []}` | see below | Noise reduction for diffing. `mask.enabled` (boolean) and `mask.exclude` (array of `iso_timestamp`, `unix_timestamp`, `relative_time`, `counter`, `uuid`, `session_token`, `tracking_param`, `cache_buster`, `resource_hash`, `iframe_marker`). |

`schedule` is a **nested object**: `schedule_interval` and `schedule_cron` used to
exist as top-level fields and are rejected — use `schedule`.

The body is accepted as JSON or form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).
With form encoding, `schedule`, `headers` and `mask` are JSON object strings and
`diff_modes` is sent by repeating the field name (or as a JSON array string) — the
same rules as the other endpoints that accept form bodies.

If `webhook_url` is new to this account, the response additionally carries
`data.data.webhook_secret` **once**: store it. It is the HMAC key our callbacks are
signed with and it is never returned again — not by `GET /v1/watch/jobs/{id}`, not
in the list.

### Receiving callbacks

We `POST` to your address with `Content-Type: application/json`, a JSON body holding
the change event, and these headers:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Watch-Signature` | `t=` followed by unix seconds, then `,v1=` followed by a lowercase hex digest. The digest is HMAC-SHA256 over the string built from those unix seconds, a dot, then the raw request body bytes. Reject anything whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes away, and compare digests in constant time. |
| `X-Flowda-Event` | Event name; currently `watch.change_detected`. |
| `X-Flowda-Event-Id` | Stable idempotency key for job, check and event; use it to deduplicate deliveries. |
| `X-Flowda-Delivery-Id` | Identifier of this delivery. |
| `X-Flowda-Attempt` | Attempt number, starting at `1`. |

Verify over the **raw body bytes you received**: parsing the JSON and serializing it
again changes the bytes and breaks the signature. Answer 2xx quickly. A non-2xx
answer is retried, up to 6 delivery attempts in total, with delays of 10s, 1m, 5m,
30m and 2h between them; 4xx answers other than 408, 425 and 429 stop immediately,
and `Retry-After` is honoured up to 10 minutes.

The body is a `watch.change_detected` event: the job and check identifiers, a
one-line `data.check.diff_summary`, and the change itself under `data.diff`. Its
schema is the `changeDetected` callback of this operation; `data.delivered_at` is
when the platform created the event, which is not the timestamp in the signature
header.

patch.description:
Partial update with the same field set as creation, **except `url`** (a job's
target cannot be changed).

* A field you leave out is unchanged.
* `webhook_url: null` (or `""`) removes the callback.
* `schedule: null` is rejected — pass a new schedule object instead.
* Changing `selector_type` without `selector` re-validates the existing selector
  against the new type.
* Re-sending the same values succeeds idempotently.
* Registering a callback address this account has not used before returns
  `data.data.webhook_secret` once, exactly like creation; the rest of the response
  is the job, nested as `data.data.job`.

The body is accepted as JSON or form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).
With form encoding, `schedule`, `headers` and `mask` are JSON object strings and
`diff_modes` is sent by repeating the field name (or as a JSON array string) — the
same rules as the other endpoints that accept form bodies.

post.description:
Runs one check synchronously (the fetch platform allows about 60 seconds) and
returns the check result, including the diff when something changed.

Unlike every other Watch endpoint the result is **flat**: `data` is
`{success, request_id, credits_used, meta, diff}`. Job details, the job list and the
check history nest the platform body one level deeper, as
`data.data.{job|jobs|checks}`.

`meta.is_baseline: true` means this was the first successful fetch: it only
establishes the baseline, so `changed` is `false` and `diff` is `null`.

Costs 1 / 3 / 5 credits according to the strategy used; a failed fetch costs 0.

409.description:
The job is paused (`details: ["The job is paused."]`) or a check is already

get.description:
Lists past checks of a job, newest first. Query parameters: `limit`
(`1 … 200`, default `50`) and `cursor` (from `data.data.next_cursor`).

List items carry `diff_summary` (human-readable, for example
`1 line modified`) but no diff body — fetch a single check for that.
The counts are nested as `data.data`: `data.data.checks` is `null` when the job has
no history, and `data.data.next_cursor` is `null` on the last page.
